criterion_notes.c1: Focuses on the overall regional sustainability status of clean water treatment plant (IPAB) provision in Soppeng Regency rather than examining household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain literal wording of Criterion 2, the study touches on legal, institutional, and tariff attributes because one of the five RAPFISH dimensions is 'Law and Institutional' (listing attributes such as availability of water management legislation, customary/religious law instruments, stakeholder communication networks, and inter-regional integrated management) and the 'Economy' dimension lists 'PDAM water tariff' and 'price discrimination among and within consumer groups' as expert-scored attributes. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading, however, Criterion 2 is NOT met ('no'): these items are merely unanalysed checklist inputs scored by experts to construct a composite treatment-plant sustainability index, with macro-governance/management background dominating the legal dimension and no empirical analysis of how any specific tariff, eligibility, documentation, tenure, or regulatory rule governs service access. Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the paper is still excluded because it fails Criteria 1, 4, and 5.
criterion_notes.c3: Uses an expert survey (purposive sampling via in-depth interviews and observation) analysed with a RAPFISH-adapted Multidimensional Scaling (MDS) ordination, leverage analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports only composite sustainability index scores (45.64% overall and five dimensional sub-indices) and root-mean-square leverage sensitivity scores for IPAB provision; it does not measure or report any outcome of household or community water access, connection, service availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: Study design is a rapid appraisal (RAPFISH/MDS) expert survey at the regency level, but the number and profile of expert respondents and raw attribute values are not reported, and no household/community population or service-access outcome is linked to an identifiable legal/administrative exposure.

evidence_quotes.quote: This study aims to look at the sustainability index of clean water supply through clean water treatment plant (known as IPAB) in Soppeng.

This study was conducted using a survey method through in-depth interviews and observation techniques. Respondents were taken by purposive random sampling with criteria of experts who have expertise in accordance with the field under study [2].

evidence_quotes.page: PDF Page 7, Section 3. Sustainability Status of Law and Institutional Dimension
evidence_quotes.quote: Based on the results of leverage analysis, attributes that are sensitive to the legal and institutional dimension of the sustainability index are obtained, namely (1) communication networks between stakeholders in the development of the clean water sector, (2) implementation of periodic clean water consumption analysis, and (3) integrated management, sharing or merger between regions.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF Page 7, Section 3. Multidimensional Sustainability Status
evidence_quotes.quote: The results of the multi-dimensional sustainability Rap-IPABSoppeng analysis in Soppeng Regency for the provision of clean water treatment plants based on existing conditions, obtained a sustainability index value of 45.64% and included in the less sustainable status.

raw_response.exposure: 48 expert-scored attributes across five dimensions (environmental, economic, social, infrastructure and technology, and law and institutional) of clean water treatment plant (IPAB) provision
raw_response.outcome: Multidimensional sustainability index values (%) and root-mean-square attribute sensitivity (leverage) scores for clean water treatment plant (IPAB) provision
raw_response.population_and_sample: Purposively sampled experts assessing clean water treatment plant (IPAB) provision in Soppeng Regency, South Sulawesi Province, Indonesia (sample size of experts not reported)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded (E04: Wrong outcome). This paper applies a RAPFISH-adapted Multidimensional Scaling (MDS) rapid appraisal of expert ratings across 48 attributes in five dimensions to compute a composite sustainability index (45.64%) for clean water treatment plant (IPAB) provision in Soppeng Regency, Indonesia. It does not report any empirical outcome measuring household or community water service access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion (failing Criterion 4), nor does it examine how a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism governs household/community access under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 scope (and even under the plain wording of Criterion 2 it remains excluded for lacking any service-access outcome and omitting basic sample details).
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional expert rapid appraisal survey using Multidimensional Scaling (RAPFISH/Rap-IPABSoppeng), leverage analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation
